turn_text: I'm Ben Domenette. You're listening to Fox News Radio. I had the opportunity to talk today to Senator Tommy Tuberville. He has been at the center of a controversy that's been playing out over the past several months. regarding his hold on a number of different promotions within the Pentagon structure. Obviously this has affected a number of different military promotions and he's been getting increasing pressure from the pro-military wing of the party and of the Senate over the fact that he's refusing to allow these promotions to go forward. Now just to put this in perspective, Any senator has the ability to put a hold on legislation or on these promotions, and it's because, you know, essentially in the modern era, they don't expect for senators to sit in their seats the whole time. They can simply dictate that, you know, hey, if I was there, I would, you know, put a rejection of unanimous consent on this type of promotion, and it effectively works as a hold. Do we see it all over the place in terms of the way that Democrats, for instance, have treated nominations under Republican presidents? In this case tommy toverville is fighting back because he believes that the pentagon has deployed a policy which is both immoral and illegal as regards their funding of abortions among members of the military in the post jobs reality by the administration decided. that rather than sort of allow the law to play out at the state level, that they would find ways to essentially go around the Hyde Amendment, which has been the policy of the United States for as long as you can probably remember, and which prohibits any kind of taxpayer funding for abortions. The way of getting around that, though, was through the form of a memo. It was not something that was a law that they passed. It was not anything that actually went through the formal process. It was not something that was included in any piece of legislation. They just decided, with a phone in a pen, as Obama used to say, that they would pay for not just the amount of time that various members of the military would take. in order to travel to get abortions, but also for their travel. And that's something that Senator Tiberville found to be objectionable. He saw that it was illegal. He saw that it was unconstitutional. It's not something that the United States of America, you know, invests in the power of the presidency to have the authority to do. And so the way that he thought that he would fight back against this is putting holds on a number of different Pentagon promotions. During peacetime, this was something that, you know, he could do with only a handful of members really pushing back against him. But obviously as things have gotten more and more heated around the world, not just the war in Ukraine, but certainly now with the conflict in Israel, the level of holds has created a situation where there are a number of different people, including people in his own party, who have gone after him for doing this. One, Senator Dan Sullivan of Alaska used remarks that were so pointed that they were actually seized upon by the Biden White House and used in social media ads against Senator Tuberville. From my perspective, this is an act of cowardice. There are actually no members of the Senate who I believe have espoused themselves as being pro-life who are really standing up with Senator Tuberville the way that they ought to be with the possible exception of Mike Lee. There are several people who have given him support where small notes of support over the course of this period, but really they ought to be lockstep on this issue. It's clearly a violation of law, and even if you aren't pro-life or strongly pro-life, it's something that you should be opposed to if you believe in constitutional government. Now, Senator Tuberville has had the screws put to him in terms of the pushback from the Republican conference. They believe that they're going to put him in a position where essentially he's incapable to maintain these holes, that they have a situation where they're willing to compromise with Democrats. in order to get around them, including potentially a nuclear option to allow these nominations to move forward. I want to say again, these holds, by the way, they do not prevent the promotions. They simply prevent the Senate from promoting these people via unanimous consent, meaning that they would have to go through the whole process of actually debating and voting on each of these promotions, as opposed to just giving them a rubber stamp. In other words, they would have to work. They would have had to stay here in August, as opposed to going back home and raising money. The Senate is notoriously opposed to having to do the work of any kind. And therefore, they find Senator Tuberville in his freshman way, incredibly infuriating. So, Senator Tuberville talked to me about the situation, about his plans going forward, his anticipation of a lawsuit against the Pentagon and others, you know, within the authority system that have allowed this illegal activity to take place, and what he expects going forward. We also talked about this season of college football, the Michigan scandal, what he expects to see from the coming college playoff and more. Senator Tommy Tuberville coming up next.
